newsitem.title: TURKEY: Borusan to partly float investment arm.
newsitem.headline: Borusan to partly float investment arm.

text.p: Turkish industrial Borusan group will float 30 percent of the share capital of its investment unit Borusan Yatirim ve Pazarlama A.S. in a two-day offer from Thursday, lead manager Ata Securities said.

The company will issue 150 billion lira of share capital and raise the total amount of share capital to 500 billion lira from 350 billion. It will sell the newly issued shares at a fixed price of 5,500 lira per 1,000 lira nominal-valued share.
Of the total 150 million shares on offer, 90 million will be allocated to domestic investors and 60 million to foreigners, the group's distributor agencies and domestic institutional investors.
Borusan Yatirim holds equity stakes of between 11.7 and 50 percent in seven group companies active in iron and steel, automotive sectors and foreign trade.
The company reported 92.4 billion lira of net profits last year and 251.5 billion lira in the first half of 1996.
Borusan group is the distributor of BMW AG cars and Caterpillar construction machinery in Turkey. It recently became the Caterpillar representative for Georgia and Azerbaijan as well.
Borusan Yatirim will be the second group firm to go public after leading steel pipe producer Borusan Birlesik Boru Fabrikalari listed part of its shares on the Istanbul Stock Exchange two years ago.
Offer co-leader is Finansbank and the consortium consists of Interbank, Korfezbank, Tutunbank, Sumerbank, Tekstilbank and brokerage houses Eczacibasi, Ekinciler and Evgin.
Branches of biggest private commercial Akbank will also act as sale agents in the offer.
